context.title: All Israel Rallies to David
context.summary: Warriors from every tribe join David, first while he is a fugitive at Ziklag and in the wilderness, then in huge numbers at Hebron to make him king.
context.background: Ziklag was a town the Philistine king Achish gave David while he hid from Saul (1 Samuel 27:6). Some of the first to join him were Benjamites, Saul's own relatives (v. 2). The chapter ends with three days of feasting at Hebron.

customs.note: In the first month (spring), the Jordan ran high with rain and snowmelt, making the crossing a real feat.

watchFor: Amasai, moved by the Spirit: 'Thine are we, David' (v. 18).
The men of Issachar 'had understanding of the times' (v. 32).

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Kish
people.summary: A Benjamite, the son of Abiel, and father of king Saul (1 Sam. 9:1, 3; 10:11, 21; 14:51; 2 Sam. 21:14). All that is recorded of him is that he sent his son Saul in search of his asses that had strayed, and that he was buried in Zelah.

people.name: Saul
people.summary: The son of Kish (probably his only son, and a child of prayer, “asked for”), of the tribe of Benjamin, the first king of the Jewish nation. The singular providential circumstances connected with his election as king are recorded in 1 Sam. 8-10.

people.name: Benjamin
people.summary: The younger son of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 35:18). His birth took place at Ephrath, on the road between Bethel and Bethlehem, at a short distance from the latter place.

people.name: Ahiezer
people.summary: The chief of the Benjamite slingers that repaired to David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

people.name: Berachah
people.summary: One of the Benjamite warriors, Saul’s brethren, who joined David when at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

people.name: Jehu
people.summary: One of the Benjamite slingers that joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

people.name: Jeziel
people.summary: Assembled by God, a son of Azmaveth.

people.name: Joash
people.summary: One of the Benjamite archers who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

people.name: Pelet
people.summary: A Benjamite who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

people.name: Shemaah
people.summary: Rumour, a Benjamite whose sons “came to David to Ziklag” (1 Chr. 12:3).

people.name: Ismaiah
people.summary: A Gibeonite who joined David at Ziklag, “a hero among the thirty and over the thirty” (1 Chr. 12:4).

people.name: Jahaziel
people.summary: Warrior among The Thirty.

people.name: Jeremiah
people.summary: A Benjamite slinger who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:4).

people.name: Johanan
people.summary: Member of the Thirty.

people.name: Josabad
people.summary: One of the Benjamite archers who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:4).

people.name: Bealiah
people.summary: Whose Lord is Jehovah, a Benjamite, one of David’s thirty heroes of the sling and bow (1 Chr. 12:5).

people.name: Jerimoth
people.summary: A Benjamite slinger who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:5).

people.name: Shemariah
people.summary: One who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:5).

people.name: Shephatiah
people.summary: A Benjamite who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:5).

people.name: Azareel
people.summary: An Aaronite of the family of Korah.

people.name: Elkanah
people.summary: The sons of Korah were Assir, Elkanah and Abiasaph. These were the Korahite clans.

people.name: Jashobeam
people.summary: This is the list of David’s mighty warriors: Jashobeam, a Hakmonite, was chief of the officers ; he raised his spear against three hundred men, whom he killed in one encounter.

people.name: Joezer
people.summary: Jehovah is his help, one of the Korhites who became part of David’s body-guard (1 Chr. 12:6).

people.name: Jeroham
people.summary: 1 Chr. 12:7; a Benjamite.

people.name: Joelah
people.summary: A Benjamite who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:7).

people.name: Zebadiah
people.summary: Sons of Jeroham.

people.name: Eliab
people.summary: One of the Gadite heroes who joined David in his stronghold in the wilderness (1 Chr. 12:9).

people.name: Obadiah
people.summary: A Gadite who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:9).

people.name: Jeremiah
people.summary: A Gadite who joined David in the wilderness (1 Chr. 12:10).

people.name: Mishmannah
people.summary: Fatness, one of the Gadite heroes who gathered to David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:10).

people.name: Attai
people.summary: The sixth.

people.name: Eliel
people.summary: A Gadite who joined David in the hold at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:11).

people.name: Johanan
people.summary: One of the Gadite heroes who joined David in the desert of Judah (1 Chr. 12:12).

people.name: Jeremiah
people.summary: A Gadite warrior (1 Chr. 12:13).

people.name: Gad
people.summary: Jacob’s seventh son, by Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid, and the brother of Asher (Gen. 30:11-13; 46:16, 18).

people.name: Jesse
people.summary: Firm, or a gift, a son of Obed, the son of Boaz and Ruth (Ruth 4:17, 22; Matt. 1:5, 6; Luke 3:32). He was the father of eight sons, the youngest of whom was David (1 Sam. 17:12).

people.name: Amasai
people.summary: The leader of a body of men who joined David in the “stronghold,” probably of Adullam (1 Chr. 12:18).

people.name: Manasseh
people.summary: The elder of the two sons of Joseph. He and his brother Ephraim were afterwards adopted by Jacob as his own sons (48:1).

people.name: Adnah
people.summary: A chief of the tribe of Manasseh who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:20).

people.name: Elihu
people.summary: One of the captains of thousands of Manasseh who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:20).

people.name: Jediael
people.summary: Men of Manasseh.

people.name: Jozabad
people.summary: A chief of the tribe of Manasseh, who defected to David.

people.name: Michael
people.summary: A Manassite, “a captain of thousands” who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:20).

people.name: Zilthai
people.summary: One of the captains of the tribe of Manasseh who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:20).

people.name: Simeon
people.summary: The second son of Jacob by Leah (Gen. 29:33). He was associated with Levi in the terrible act of vengeance against Hamor and the Shechemites (34:25, 26).

people.name: Levi
people.summary: The third son of Jacob by Leah. The origin of the name is found in Leah’s words (Gen. 29:34), “This time will my husband be joined [Heb. yillaveh] unto me.”

people.name: Jehoiada
people.summary: The father of Benaiah, who was one of David’s chief warriors (2 Sam. 8:18; 20:23).

people.name: Zadok
people.summary: A son of Ahitub, of the line of Eleazer (2 Sam. 8:17; 1 Chr. 24:3), high priest in the time of David (2 Sam. 20:25) and Solomon (1 Kings 4:4).

people.name: Ephraim
people.summary: Double fruitfulness (“for God had made him fruitful in the land of his affliction”). The second son of Joseph, born in Egypt (Gen. 41:52; 46:20).

people.name: Issachar
people.summary: Hired (Gen. 30:18). “God hath given me,” said Leah, “my hire (Heb. sekhari)...and she called his name Issachar.” He was Jacob’s ninth son, and was born in Padan-aram (comp. 28:2).

people.name: Zebulun
people.summary: Dwelling, the sixth and youngest son of Jacob and Leah (Gen. 30:20). Little is known of his personal history.

people.name: Naphtali
people.summary: My wrestling, the fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s handmaid (Gen. 30:8). When Jacob went down into Egypt, Naphtali had four sons (Gen. 46:24).

people.name: Asher
people.summary: Happy, Jacob’s eigth son; his mother was Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid (Gen. 30:13). Of the tribe founded by him nothing is recorded beyond its holding a place in the list of the tribes (35:26; 46:17; Ex. 1:4, etc.) It increased in numbers twenty-nine percent, during the thirty-eight years’ wanderings.

places.name: Ziklag
places.summary: A town in the Negeb, or south country of Judah (Josh. 15:31), in the possession of the Philistines when David fled to Gath from Ziph with all his followers.

places.name: Gederah
places.summary: The fortress; a fortified place, a town in the plain (shephelah) of Judah (Josh. 15:36). This is a very common Canaanite and Phoenician name.

places.name: Gibeon
places.summary: Hill-city, “one of the royal cities, greater than Ai, and all the men thereof were mighty” (Josh. 10:2). Its inhabitants were Hivites (11:19).

places.name: Gedor
places.summary: A town apparently in Benjamin (1 Chr. 12:7), the same probably as Geder (Josh. 12:13).

places.name: Jordan
places.summary: But besides these two historical fountains there is a third, called the Hasbany, which rises in the bottom of a valley at the western base of Hermon, 12 miles north of Tell-el-Kady.

places.name: Hebron
places.summary: A city in the south end of the valley of Eshcol, about midway between Jerusalem and Beersheba, from which it is distant about 20 miles in a straight line.
